briefing:
Day 15 concludes with the crisis firmly in its diplomatic endgame. The Istanbul II summit — now scheduled for Day 21-22 — has become the focal point for all parties. Russia's nuclear transparency offer and gas restoration create genuine diplomatic momentum, but also risk splitting Western consensus between hawks who want to maintain maximum pressure and pragmatists who see an off-ramp.

The European Three (UK-France-Germany) coordination marks a significant new dynamic — for the first time, major European NATO allies are explicitly coordinating to prevent a US-Russia bilateral deal that excludes them. France's ESAF and Germany's Geneva Track 2 hosting represent institutional alternatives to Trump's dealmaking.

Military posture remains stable. No combat operations. All forces in garrison or defensive positions. The Suwalki Shield Force is fully operational. Poland's Shield East fortifications continue advancing. Nordic NORDEFCO implementation proceeds. Baltic Defense Council deepens integration.

Three key events will dominate the next 24 hours: (1) Hungarian confidence vote on Day 16 — Orban's political survival hangs in the balance; (2) First CJCS-Gerasimov military hotline call — unprecedented direct channel; (3) Countdown to IAEA arrival in Belarus on Day 17. Markets respond positively — oil drops to $80.50 on combined summit and gas restoration optimism.
narrative:
Day 15 of the Suwalki Gap Crisis marks a decisive pivot from post-conflict consolidation to active summit diplomacy. In a surprising move that catches Western intelligence off-guard, Russia announces it will permit limited IAEA inspection of its Kaliningrad nuclear inventory — not full 'international custody' as Moscow's initial trial balloon suggested, but supervised assessment of tactical weapons with IAEA monitors present. This partial transparency gambit is designed to give Putin a 'responsible nuclear power' narrative heading into Istanbul II. Simultaneously, Gazprom begins technical preparations to restore 15% of normal gas flows to the EU, with first deliveries expected within 48 hours — a tangible economic olive branch that immediately splits European opinion on sanctions continuation.

The European response crystallizes around a fear of marginalization. An emergency UK-France-Germany coordination call produces the 'European Three' framework — a joint demand that Istanbul II include formal European representation, not just a US-Russia bilateral. Macron activates ESAF as Europe's counter-framework, while Germany announces an EUR 8B emergency defense supplemental and offers Berlin as host for Geneva Process Track 2 on security architecture. The message to Washington is clear: Europe will not be carved up in a room with just Trump and Putin.

On the ground, the first CJCS-Gerasimov secure call is scheduled for Day 16 — the first direct military-to-military communication between US and Russian general staffs since the crisis began. The US formally launches the F-35 reinstatement process for Turkey, with an expedited review timeline. Belarus's transitional council announces that IAEA inspectors will arrive Day 17, with Western observers invited — a dramatic assertion of sovereignty over Russian nuclear weapons on Belarusian soil. In Budapest, Orban prepares for tomorrow's confidence vote with a three-pronged strategy: scapegoat intelligence chief Benko, offer limited EU concessions, and seek Turkish endorsement. Whether his razor-thin majority holds remains the most consequential domestic political question of the crisis.

Not a coup plan, but succession contingency planning that suggests Putin's inner circle is preparing for the possibility he cannot survive politically. The Kremlin denounces the leak as Western fabrication.

Kaliningrad Governor Alikhanov releases second video — this time directly addressing Putin on camera, documenting empty grocery stores and 12-hour power rationing for 430,000 civilians.
